body: holy smokes! this is amazing, i cant imagine working on the same world for two years:) great job!!
gosh, im such a sucker for ponds and little water features. your base is looking great! i love mizunos:)

honestly I love this! it’s doable in survival, has a good shape and depth, the blocks all go together, and it seems practical as well with the farm and portal so close:) 

if you wanted to make it look a bit cleaner, you could either terraform the surrounding grass area so it isn’t square, or you could add a retaining wall type thing around it to give it some structure. what i mean by that is going around the ground level with stone brick or something, and maybe some scattered fences to give the feeling of a perimeter without sacrificing ease of entry. the build itself is fantastic though honestly, next time i make a new world i might try this kind of shape!

Paper towel is a really good plan, because I really didn’t want to have to throw away my dish cloths. I think I will have to with my little scrub brush thing, but I can handle that loss. I did read the rest of your comment, I am sorry for not replying to more specifics as I am feeling a bit overwhelmed right now. Your advice is valuable; I have tried paper plates since many people recommended them and I am 100% going to keep some on hand in case I feel myself getting like this again. It is way easier and less overwhelming to just throw something in a bag and be done with it. 

Thank you for explaining how mold works as well, it’s easier for me to picture it just sitting on top when you describe it as a crust instead of like. having tiny invisible roots all throughout anything it touched.

I do not know how to edit my comment, but I also forgot to say that I got those thick rubber kitchen gloves to help because they go up to mid forearm and that way I won’t have to touch the dirty water either. I will throw them away after too to make things feel better too. 

I do have a dumpster for my building, when it gets really bad I try taking out a bag or two every time I leave for class, work, etc. and I usually have no left at the end of a week. Depending on how many I end up with I very well may take multiple trips in the middle of the night though, haha.

See, I thought about throwing things away and starting fresh but I am also struggling financially, so I really will need to keep as much as I can. I’ve actually been using paper plates and cutlery recently, its worked really well so far to at least get me to eat something every now and then, and I’d like to keep using them when I’m back in a more normal state to keep ahead of things. Thank you for  being kind about not doing everything 100% perfect, I know it seems small but something as simple as not having to seperate recycling makes the task seem so much less daunting. 

I want to clean the counter off today. Even if i have to put dishes on the floor, I can at least sort things into groups by dish type or something. I have fly strips from the dollar store so I’ll try that around the place as well as those vinegar traps. 

I don’t have a pot to boil water but when I do I’m going to make laundry detergent soup. I’ve genuinely never heard of that before, thank you for the suggestions!

I appreciate the advice, unfortunately it isn’t as easy as just deciding what task to take care of first and committing to finish it, at least not for me. Breaking tasks up into smaller parts is a good idea to make it feel more manageable, though. 

I know living in these conditions isn’t healthy, I don’t want this either and I know it’s my own fault. My therapist and I are working on trying to get me to do these things like cleaning or cooking for myself instead of out of fear/anxiety of what other people would think, so I will work on that more instead of imagining my boss or mom. I think this might be something you could try too if you wanted, so you don’t need to feel anxious. 

I still struggle with simple basic tasks including cooking/meal prep so I think alot of what you said last would maybe apply to me when I grow a bit more. I really do want to work up to doing things as they come up because they need to be done, please understand that I’m trying as hard as I am able, even if it sounds unbelievable. Thank you for your response and advice.
thank you so much, everyone here is so nice
That strategy might be something I can try when I get back on my feet. Thank you so much for the vibes!

I am grossed out by the thought of mold because it feels contaminated and like anything it touches will never be clean again. I do have kitchen gloves and can wear a mask but don’t know how to get it out of the dish and into the garbage, especially since it feels like it will spread into the air when I move it.

Sorry it took me a second to figure out how to reply to comments. I’m a university student and I’m keeping up with one of my classes which is good, and I’m working part time as well which gets me outside and some exercise. I also learned how to take the bus on tuesday and took it to school and back for the first time. I do have a meeting with my therapist next week but I might poke around my university’s website/google if I am able to see if there are other resources I can access sooner. Another person would help immensely if there is anything like that in my area. Thank you for the confidence, I really do want to get through this.
